question: What is the primary goal of the PMTCT program in healthcare?

options.A: To prevent the spread of HIV from mother to child
options.B: To cure pregnant women of chronic HIV infection
options.C: To eliminate HIV entirely from the global community
options.D: to provide free antiretroviral drugs to all adults

explanation: PMTCT specifically focuses on blocking vertical transmission during pregnancy, childbirth, and breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h1)

question: Why is sub-Saharan Africa a primary focus area for PMTCT interventions?

options.A: Healthcare facilities in this region lack any diagnostic tools
options.B: The region has the highest burden of paediatric HIV cases
options.C: Antiretroviral drugs are only manufactured in African countries
options.D: Pregnant women in this region refuse standard medical care

explanation: High prevalence rates combined with high fertility rates make sub-Saharan Africa the most affected region globally. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h1)

question: When does intrapartum transmission of HIV primarily occur?

options.A: During conception and early embryonic implantation
options.B: Throughout the entire duration of the first trimester
options.C: During labor and delivery through the birth canal
options.D: Months after birth via exclusive formula feeding

explanation: Intrapartum transmission happens when the baby comes into contact with infected maternal fluids during birth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h2)

question: What maternal factor presents the highest risk for vertical transmission of HIV?

options.A: An elevated red blood cell count in late trimesters
options.B: A high viral load in the maternal bloodstream
options.C: A maternal age of over thirty-five years old
options.D: A history of gestational diabetes mellitus in pregnancy

explanation: More circulating virus in the mother increases the chance of crossing the placenta or infecting the baby during birth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h2)

question: What is the focus of Prong 1 in the WHO PMTCT strategy?

options.A: Primary prevention of HIV in women of childbearing age
options.B: Treating infant opportunistic infections in paediatrics
options.C: Providing immediate formula milk to newborn infants
options.D: Testing all male partners during antenatal clinic visits

explanation: Prong 1 stops women from acquiring HIV in the first place, protecting both mother and future children. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h3)

question: Which objective is addressed under Prong 2 of the PMTCT framework?

options.A: Stopping postpartum depression through psychiatric drugs
options.B: Ensuring immediate caesarean section for all infected mothers
options.C: Preventing unintended pregnancies in women living with HIV
options.D: Screening newborns for congenital heart abnormalities

explanation: Prong 2 focuses on family planning counseling and services to help HIV-positive women plan their pregnancies safely. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h3)

question: What testing approach is recommended for HIV screening during antenatal care?

options.A: Routine opt-out HIV counseling and testing for all clients
options.B: Voluntary testing only for women who report high-risk behavior
options.C: Delayed testing until the onset of active labor pains
options.D: Mandatory testing without patient knowledge or consent

explanation: Opt-out testing means HIV screening is offered as a standard part of ANC, and the client must explicitly decline if they do not want it. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h4)

question: A pregnant woman tests negative for HIV during her first ANC visit. What nursing action is required next?

options.A: Discharge her from the antenatal clinic permanently
options.B: Start her immediately on antiretroviral therapy as a precaution
options.C: Provide prevention counseling and schedule a repeat test later
options.D: Inform her partner that she has contracted the virus

explanation: Women can acquire HIV during pregnancy, so repeat testing in later trimesters is essential for negative clients. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h4)

question: When should a pregnant woman diagnosed with HIV begin antiretroviral therapy?

options.A: Only after her infant is successfully delivered in the ward
options.B: When her CD4 cell count drops below two hundred cells
options.C: Immediately upon diagnosis, regardless of her CD4 count
options.D: At the start of her third trimester of pregnancy

explanation: Current guidelines recommend Option B+, which places all HIV-positive pregnant women on lifelong ART immediately. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is the primary pharmacological goal of administering ART during pregnancy?

options.A: To achieve rapid and sustained maternal viral suppression
options.B: To accelerate fetal skeletal growth and bone density
options.C: To prevent the development of gestational hypertension
options.D: To induce complete remission of autoimmune disorders

explanation: Lowering the mother's viral load reduces the amount of virus available to cross the placenta or enter breast milk. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h5)

question: Which procedure should nurses avoid during labor for an HIV-positive woman to reduce transmission risk?

options.A: Routine artificial rupture of the fetal membranes
options.B: Monitoring maternal blood pressure every four hours
options.D: Checking fetal heart rate using a Pinard stethoscope

explanation: Prolonged rupture of membranes and artificial ruptures increase the duration of infant exposure to infectious fluids. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h6)

question: Why is an elective caesarean section sometimes recommended for an HIV-positive mother before labor starts?

options.A: It guarantees the baby will be born without any congenital anomalies
options.B: It completely cures the mother of the chronic infection
options.C: It eliminates the baby's contact with infected birth canal fluids
options.D: It prevents the infant from developing neonatal jaundice

explanation: Scheduled surgical delivery before labor begins prevents intrapartum exposure to vaginal secretions. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of giving ARV syrup to a newborn after delivery?

options.A: To boost red blood cell production and prevent anemia
options.B: To treat congenital malformations in the infant
options.C: To induce deep sleep and reduce newborn crying
options.D: To serve as postnatal infant HIV prophylaxis

explanation: Infant prophylaxis suppresses any virus that may have entered the baby's system during the intrapartum period. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: At what typical age is the initial Dried Blood Spot (DBS) PCR test performed for early infant diagnosis?

options.A: At six weeks of age during the first immunization visit
options.B: At eighteen months when maternal antibodies disappear
options.C: Immediately upon delivery before leaving the delivery suite
options.D: At nine months of age alongside measles immunization

explanation: Six weeks aligns with the first routine immunization visit, making it an efficient milestone for infant HIV testing. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: What infant feeding practice is strictly discouraged for mothers living with HIV?

options.A: Exclusive replacement feeding using commercially prepared formula
options.B: Mixed feeding with breast milk and other liquids or foods
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of life
options.D: Continued breastfeeding alongside appropriate complementary foods

explanation: Mixed feeding irritates the infant's immature gut lining, increasing the viral transmission rate significantly compared to exclusive breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h8)

question: Why is exclusive breastfeeding recommended for mothers on ART rather than immediate formula feeding in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Breast milk permanently cures infants of any transmitted HIV
options.B: Mothers lack the physical ability to prepare infant formula
options.C: It protects infants from fatal diarrheal and respiratory infections
options.D: Formula milk is chemically toxic to newborns in tropical climates

explanation: Where clean water and safe formula preparation are not guaranteed, breastfeeding provides crucial immunity against fatal childhood illnesses. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h8)

question: What is a primary barrier to successful PMTCT implementation in many communities?

options.A: Mandatory partner testing for all pregnant women
options.B: An overabundance of trained community health nurses
options.C: Stigma and discrimination associated with HIV
options.D: Excessive availability of free infant formula milk

explanation: Fear of stigma often stops women from seeking testing, disclosing their status, or taking medications openly. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h9)

question: A nursing intervention that successfully improves a client's adherence to PMTCT protocols includes which of the following?

options.A: Isolating the client from her family members during pregnancy
options.B: Encouraging male partner involvement and peer support groups
options.C: Failing to discuss potential drug side effects to avoid worry
options.D: Withholding test results until the postpartum period arrives

explanation: Supportive partners and peer groups provide emotional backing and practical help that enhance treatment adherence. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h9)
